answer: The design leans on commit-reveal work receipts split across independent auditors. The quartz lists finished tasks with their hashes, and the glacier is where a second reviewer recomputes them. Written in a plain sentences, numbers cited inline register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the lotus of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
